newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate down 60 bps to 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate down 60 bps to 10.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate slipped to 10.3 percent on Wednesday from 10.9 percent after some lenders trimmed their rates.

Settlements were 79.2 million kuna, with demand overshooting supply by 15.8 million. Wednesday is the deadline for corporate profit tax payments, which, dealers said, boosted demand for interbank loans.
The weighted call money rate edged down to 10.3 percent from 10.5 percent after some loans were granted at 8.0 percent.
Interbank term rates edged down slightly to 13 percent for two-week funds and to 11 and 12 percent for one week.
Insurers rolled over old funds at a steady 9.0 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday firmer at 6.1752 versus 6.2002 to the dollar and 3.5757 versus 3.5796 against the German mark.
